subject: Climate & Environment
title: Pollution and Biodiversity
description: Learn Pollution and Biodiversity in one minute.

hook.text: DDT nearly wiped out bald eagles. Their eggshells thinned so much they cracked under the mother.

buildup.text: Pesticides, plastics, and chemicals accumulate in food chains — a process called bioaccumulation.

discovery.text: Top predators get the highest doses because toxins concentrate at each step up the chain.

twist.text: Microplastics are now found inside plankton, the base of the ocean food web.

climax.text: Banning DDT saved the bald eagle. But newer chemicals enter use faster than we can test them.

punchline.text: What we put into the environment comes back to us through the food chain.

quiz.question: What is bioaccumulation?
options: Toxins concentrating as they move up the food chain
Animals growing larger in polluted areas

details.summary: Chemical pollution from pesticides, plastics, heavy metals, and nutrient runoff poisons wildlife, disrupts reproduction, and degrades habitats. Eutrophication from fertilizer runoff creates ocean dead zones, while microplastics now appear in nearly every ecosystem.
details.whyItMatters: Pollution differs from habitat loss because it affects organisms even in apparently intact ecosystems. Invisible contamination can cause population crashes with no visible habitat change.
takeaways: Pesticides like neonicotinoids are devastating bee populations
Nutrient runoff creates over 400 ocean dead zones worldwide
Microplastics have been found in Arctic ice and deep-sea organisms

faq.question: What are ocean dead zones and how do they form?
faq.answer: Dead zones are areas where excessive nutrient runoff triggers algal blooms. When the algae die, bacteria decompose them and consume dissolved oxygen, suffocating fish and invertebrates. The Gulf of Mexico dead zone covers over 15,000 square kilometers.

faq.question: How do microplastics affect wildlife?
faq.answer: Animals ingest microplastics mistaking them for food, causing physical gut damage and chemical toxicity. Plastics absorb and concentrate pollutants, and they have been found in the tissues of organisms from zooplankton to whales.
